title: Alice & Bob Demonstrates Multi-Hour Physical Bit-Flip Suppression on Single-Cat and Helium 2 Processors - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Alice & Bob reported a 44-minute mean bit-flip lifetime on a single cat qubit and 189–252 minute lifetimes on its 12-qubit Helium 2 processor, empirically supporting the one-hour bit-flip baseline used in its ~45,000-qubit fault-tolerant RSA-2048 Shor model. The remaining gap is sustaining these lifetimes during bias-preserving two-qubit gates.

insights.claim: Alice & Bob measured a mean idle bit-flip lifetime of 44 minutes (95% CI: 33–60 min) on a single-qubit galvanic cat device at an average photon number of 11, over a 61-hour run with 41 quantum jumps.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hour-scale physical bit-flip lifetimes are a concrete hardware milestone for the cat-qubit approach to cheaper fault tolerance.
insights.quote: Mean bit-flip lifetime: 44 minutes (95% CI: 33–60 min) over 61 hours (41 quantum jumps).
insights.locator: Alice & Bob Experimental Cat-Qubit Hardware Benchmarks

insights.claim: On Alice & Bob's 12-qubit Helium 2 processor, operated at 11 to 16 photons, individual cat qubits showed bit-flip lifetimes of 189 minutes (Cat 1), 252 minutes (Cat 8) and 189 minutes (Cat 12).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multi-qubit arrays exceeding three hours suggest the result is not a single-device fluke and may scale across a processor.
insights.quote: Cat 1: 189 min | Cat 8: 252 min | Cat 12: 189 min bit-flip lifetimes.
insights.locator: Alice & Bob Experimental Cat-Qubit Hardware Benchmarks

insights.claim: Statistical analysis of the 41 quantum-jump events showed single-exponential, memoryless Poisson statistics consistent with Markovian switching, indicating bit flips behave as a well-modeled random process.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Memoryless, well-characterized errors are easier to correct with codes, de-risking the error model behind resource estimates.
insights.quote: Autocorrelation and Bayesian analysis confirmed single-exponential, memoryless Poisson statistics consistent with Markovian switching.

insights.claim: Cat qubits use two-photon dissipation to exponentially suppress bit-flip errors at the cost of linearly increasing phase-flip noise, creating a deliberate noise bias.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The bias trade-off is the core architectural bet that lets cat-qubit vendors claim far lower qubit overheads than conventional approaches.
insights.quote: using two-photon dissipation to exponentially suppress bit-flip errors at the cost of linearly increasing phase-flip noise

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's single cat qubit showed a phase-flip lifetime of only 420 ns (equivalent to a single-photon T1 of 9.2 μs), orders of magnitude shorter than its bit-flip lifetime.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The extreme asymmetry means phase-flip correction still carries the burden, so investors should track phase-flip metrics, not just headline bit-flip times.
insights.quote: Phase-flip lifetime of 420 ns (equivalent to single-photon T1 = 9.2 μs).
insights.locator: Alice & Bob Experimental Cat-Qubit Hardware Benchmarks

insights.claim: Alice & Bob demonstrated continuous Z rotations with a Z-gate fidelity of 94.2% executed in 26.5 ns, to show that macroscopic bit-flip stability did not compromise quantum coherence.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 94.2% single-qubit gate fidelity is modest, signaling that gate quality remains an engineering gap alongside lifetimes.
insights.quote: Z-gate fidelity of 94.2% executed in 26.5 ns.
insights.locator: Alice & Bob Experimental Cat-Qubit Hardware Benchmarks

themes.theme: Implications for Shor's algorithm resource estimates

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's idealized Shor compilation assumed an unmitigated 100-year bit-flip lifetime to factor RSA-2048 on 22,593 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The headline ~23,000-qubit figure depends on an idealized assumption far beyond what hardware currently shows.
insights.quote: assumed an unmitigated 100-year bit-flip lifetime to factor RSA-2048 on 22,593 qubits

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's fault-tolerant model showed a physical bit-flip rate of once per hour could be corrected by concatenating cat qubits into an outer distance-3 bit-flip code, roughly doubling the required processor to about 45,000 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A realistic RSA-2048 threat estimate for cat qubits is ~45,000 qubits, a key input for post-quantum cryptography timelines.
insights.quote: expanding the required processor size to roughly 45,000 qubits

insights.claim: The Helium 2 results confirm that physical cat-qubit devices can operate within the one-hour concatenation threshold during idle periods, providing empirical backing for the error-model assumptions of the 45,000-qubit fault-tolerant estimate.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Validating model assumptions with hardware strengthens the credibility of Alice & Bob's roadmap versus competing modalities.
insights.quote: The demonstration confirms that physical devices can operate within this concatenation threshold during idle periods

insights.claim: Sustaining hour-scale bit-flip lifetimes during two-qubit entangling operations such as bias-preserving CNOT gates remains the next milestone before Alice & Bob can realize active logical error correction.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The idle-only nature of the result means the key de-risking event for investors is still ahead: bias-preserving CNOT performance.
insights.quote: sustaining these lifetimes during two-qubit entangling operations (such as bias-preserving CNOT gates) remains the next milestone
